title: Air India Launches Only Direct Toronto-Mumbai Flight for Winter Season
excerpt: Seasonal AI193/AI192 service runs three times weekly from October 25 to March 26 on an upgraded Boeing 777-300ER, adding nearly 2,000 seats a week between Canada and India.
body:
• Air India has inaugurated the only direct flight between Toronto Pearson (YYZ) and Mumbai (BOM), a seasonal service running from October 25, 2026 to March 26, 2027.
  • The route operates three times a week — Wednesday, Friday and Sunday — on an upgraded Boeing 777-300ER as AI193 Mumbai-Toronto and AI192 Toronto-Mumbai, adding nearly 2,000 seats a week.
  • Reader utility: Book AI193/AI192 for Wed/Fri/Sun travel between Oct 25 and Mar 26 on Air India website or app; from Mumbai you can connect onward to Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kochi and other Indian cities.
  • Air India now operates 20 weekly flights between India and Canada this winter, and premium seat capacity to Toronto rises 71 percent.

Air India’s new flight between Toronto Pearson and Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport has taken off, giving the two cities their only direct air link this winter. The inaugural service was marked at Toronto Pearson in the presence of Mahaveer Singhvi, Consul General of India in Toronto, alongside travel trade partners and airline and airport staff, according to TravelPulse Canada.

The route matters because demand was already there without a non-stop option. OAG estimates 128,000 round-trip passengers travelled between Mumbai and Toronto between June 2025 and May 2026. Until now those travellers had to connect through Delhi or a third hub. Air India says it is the only carrier operating direct flights between the two cities during the winter 2026-27 season.

Schedule, aircraft and seats

The seasonal service runs three times a week from October 25, 2026 through March 26, 2027. TravelPulse lists AI193 departing Mumbai at 00:25 and arriving in Toronto at 11:00 on Wednesday, Friday and Sunday, with AI192 departing Toronto at 13:30 and arriving in Mumbai at 14:10 the next day, all times local. Travellers should confirm timings for their exact date when booking, as long-haul schedules can shift across the winter season.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Degje__jm7X/

"The route matters because demand was already there without a non-stop option."

Flights use an upgraded Boeing 777-300ER with eight First Class suites with privacy sliding doors, 40 fully flat beds in Business Class and 280 Economy seats, with Wi-Fi in all cabins. The route adds nearly 2,000 seats each week between Canada and India, Air India said in its inauguration coverage and press release.

“This new route is an important addition to Toronto Pearson’s growing global network, providing the only direct connection between Toronto and Mumbai, India’s financial capital,” said Kurush Minocher, Chief Commercial Officer, Toronto Pearson. “The service will strengthen connectivity for travellers, support business and trade between Canada and India.”

A wider Canada upgrade

Mumbai is the second Toronto gateway in a broader winter expansion. Air India operates 10 weekly Delhi-Toronto flights, seven of them on its brand-new Boeing 787-9 and three initially on the 777-300ER before transitioning to the 787-9 from January 2027. With seven weekly Delhi-Vancouver flights, the airline totals 20 weekly flights between India and Canada this winter.

Overall capacity between India and Canada rises by 4,400 seats a month, and premium seat capacity to Toronto rises 71 percent. From January 2027, Air India says, all its flights from Toronto Pearson will feature new or significantly upgraded cabin interiors.

“Canada is one of Air India’s most important international markets, with deep people-to-people connections driving strong demand for travel, particularly during the festive and holiday season,” said Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India.

What it means for travellers

For families in the Greater Toronto Area travelling to Maharashtra and western India, the flight removes a Delhi transit or a Gulf or European stop on the busiest winter dates. Through Mumbai, Air India offers onward connections to Ahmedabad, Amritsar, Bengaluru, Chandigarh, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kochi, Ludhiana and Vadodara, among other cities. The seasonal window ends March 26, 2027, so travellers planning spring trips should check whether a Delhi connection or another routing fits their dates better.
